recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-43164 unless the work group later decides to broaden the displayed short/definition text beyond the current value set code labels.
issue_request: FHIR-43164 was an Applied, Persuasive with Modification OO change request for R6. It asked to change DeviceDefinition.deviceName.type from a required code binding to an extensible binding that permits additional name types, add jurisdictional guidance for choosing the registered-name, and apply the same change to Device.name.type.
initial_application: The change was applied in two Jira-tagged commits. fe02a2c70b changed DeviceDefinition.deviceName.type to CodeableConcept, set the DeviceNameType binding strength to extensible, and added the registered-name jurisdiction comment. After Jira QA noted that Device.name.type had been missed, 744c0f6283 made the same CodeableConcept/extensible/comment change for Device.name.type.
additional_context: Device and DeviceDefinition are active current-build resources in source/fhir.ini. Current source still carries the requested binding strength, datatype, and comment on both elements. The OO 2023-11-30 and 2023-12-07 Confluence minutes show FHIR-43164 in the OO block-vote trail with the same 7-0-5 vote recorded in Jira. FHIR-43165 appeared in the same block vote but concerns DeviceDefinition.material.substance, is already represented on the combined branch, and does not change the FHIR-43164 conclusion.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The authoritative StructureDefinition source for both DeviceDefinition.deviceName.type and Device.name.type already matches the applied resolution, including the jurisdictional registered-name clarification and extensible DeviceNameType binding.
